title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking at any temperature in a local one-dimensional model
abstract: We present a one-dimensional classical statistical physics model on an infinite lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions and local state space $\mathbb{Z}^2$, with a ``helical" symmetry group $\mathbb{Z}^2\rtimes \mathbb{Z}$ mixing flavor symmetry with spatial translation. For any $0<β<\infty$, we construct an uncountable infinity of DLR (Gibbs) states parameterized by $\mathbb{R}^2$, with a free $\mathbb{Z}^2$ flavor symmetry group action; as such, we interpret the model as exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking at any temperature. The most general DLR state we construct is interpreted as an infinite sequence of localized domain walls separating a pair of asymptotic ``symmetry sectors". Although any normalizable Gibbs state necessarily breaks a countably infinite freely-acting symmetry group, a natural regularization of the problem to (arbitrarily) large but finite systems with periodic boundary conditions has measure concentration in disjoint and far-separated symmetry-related clusters in the (now unique) Gibbs state, which justifies our interpretation of spontaneous symmetry breaking on the infinite line. A modification of the model with local state space $\mathbb{R}^2$ must break a continuous helical symmetry at any temperature. This is not a contradiction with the Mermin-Wagner Theorem, because this continuous helical symmetry is non-compact and does not commute with translation.
summary: This paper analyzes a 1D classical statistical model with a helical symmetry, demonstrating that it exhibits spontaneous symmetry breaking at any temperature. This is achieved by constructing an uncountable infinity of distinct Gibbs states using the DLR formalism. The work highlights how the infinite nature of the state space allows the model to circumvent standard theorems that restrict SSB to higher dimensions.
main_problem: To investigate the possibility of spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) at any finite, positive temperature in a local one-dimensional model, challenging standard theorems that forbid such breaking in 1D systems.
main_result: The authors construct an uncountable infinity of Gibbs states, demonstrating that the model exhibits spontaneous symmetry breaking at any temperature due to the structure of the state space.
method: The analysis relies on the DLR formalism and transfer matrix methods to characterize the Gibbs states and analyze the measure concentration phenomenon.
model_or_system: The model is a classical statistical physics system on an infinite 1D lattice ($\mathbb{Z}$) with a local state space ($\mathbb{Z}^2$ or $\mathbb{Z}_2$), governed by nearest-neighbor interactions and possessing a helical symmetry group.
key_observables: The existence and number of distinct DLR (Gibbs) states, and the measure concentration into symmetry-related clusters.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), the hyperbolic matrix $A \in SL(2, \mathbb{Z})$, and the parameters $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$ labeling the distinct states.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the countably infinite on-site state space allows for a loophole in standard theorems that forbid thermal SSB in 1D.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the model and symmetries, constructing the manifold of Gibbs states using the DLR formalism, and then rigorously arguing that the measure concentration into distinct symmetry sectors implies SSB.
why_interesting: The work challenges fundamental theorems in 1D statistical mechanics by exploiting the structure of the state space, providing a theoretical framework for when and how SSB can occur in low dimensions.
